parts:
Done. Here's where things stand.

**Review of investigations-2 and the arithmetic_source_audit.** The portfolio setup is coherent, and the two Codex audits in arithmetic_source_audit are careful: the October 5 source is pinned by hash, the cube-tail branch ledger verifies a strictly decreasing row scale and the signed preimage cancellation, and the theta audit reaches the Appendix A.2 argument with explicit version correspondence. I re-ran the regrouping checker (729 cases, 4,913 preimages, 65 child checks); the record matches apart from path/software fields. Claims are properly labelled conditional on `prop:R` and the imported sieve/theta theorems, and the next target (initial Poisson reduction) is the right one. One small thing to harmonize: the notes say "GPT-6, effort not exposed" while the READMEs say "GPT-6-astra, ultra".

**Newman certificate audit — first bounded task completed, with a negative benchmark.** I pinned the Gomila package (commit `a74738de…`, claim Λ ≤ 0.1787854 via Polymath Theorem 1.2 at X = 6000000185827, t₀ = 129/800, y₀² = 87677/2500000), verified its 443-file seal, and wrote a dependency ledger for its four lanes. An independent float64 reimplementation of the finite lane reproduces the stored floors at every first-of-run row to all six stored digits (weakest row 7.913667e-7 vs stored 0.000000791366), and a 50-digit standard-library replay of the Theorem 1.3 error budget agrees with the package's Arb values. The decisive finding: the only cells where the approximation error matters are the first finite rows (T ≈ 7.9e-7 vs E_max = 2.33e-7), but that lane is uniform in x, so the repository's pointwise corrected interface cannot enter it at all; and even if it could, the measured slopes (∂L/∂y² = 9.5, ∂L/∂t = 19) cap the gain at ΔΛ ≈ 1.2e-8. The barrier's 883 prisms have margins 400× the approximation allowance. So the README's stop condition is met: the corrected interface changes neither feasibility nor cost for this certificate class.

One side observation worth your attention: the package's own producer has an unused "sharp" weight (Polymath §8.5 improved triangle inequality) that gives L = 0.077 at the certified row instead of 7.9e-7, moving the lane boundary by roughly 0.004–0.006 in Λ — the real lever in this certificate class is the lower-bound lemma, not the Riemann–Siegel error term. I did not pursue it (it would need the package's y-transfer re-proved for that weight).

Files are in `papers/investigations-2/newman_certificate_audit/` (two notes, two scripts, two JSON records, README updates) plus one status sentence in the portfolio README — nothing committed to git. The replay tool needs numpy (1.6e9 terms) and is flagged as a benchmark, not a check programme; the error-budget checker is standard-library and replays identically on your machine. A session summary is saved in the project as `claude/newman-certificate-audit-session-2026-10-12.md`.

archive_metadata.format: ChatGPT-style conversation mapping; local conversion, not an official provider export
archive_metadata.source_kind: Claude Cowork cloud session event log (claude.ai GET /v1/code/sessions/{id}/events), read in the signed-in browser and reduced to completed public messages
archive_metadata.message_timestamps: Event times, in seconds since Unix epoch and ISO 8601: the session's own timestamp where the event carries one, otherwise the server's event time (typed messages); the conversation create_time is the session's creation time in the session list
archive_metadata.coverage: Messages typed by the person (including any sent while a reply was in progress, with the names of files sent with them) and interruption markers; the options the person selected in question cards; the assistant text shown in the chat: progress lines between tool calls, question cards rendered as text, notes and file-card captions sent through tools (phase commentary), and the text ending each completed turn (phase final_answer); recorded through the event log as read
omitted_record_types: system, developer and harness text (reminders, date notes, memory snapshots, continuation summaries, hook feedback, skill text, local command output)
tool calls and outputs, except the chat-visible items named in coverage
permission prompts, control and environment events, usage and cost figures
attachment contents (file names are kept in message metadata)

session.title_source: the session's title in the Cowork session list

source_events.read_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) in Claude Cowork, via Claude in Chrome
source_events.note: sha256_of_events_json is the SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(events sorted by sequence_num) computed in the browser; neither the event log nor the events file is stored in the repository, since they hold instructions, reasoning and tool traffic that the coverage rules exclude

archive_metadata.delivered_files_note: Paths reported by device_commit_files and names of file cards; files written by shell commands or saved as project documents are not detected
